messages:
Incidents Bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: elevated 5xx rate for model-runner in us-west-2 (service: hosted-api). Current error rate ~12% over last 5m. Pager: Maya (oncall). Runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/model-runner-5xx

Maya (oncall): Acked. Investigating now. Sam / Jit can you pull logs and dmesg from the failing nodes? Any recent deploys?

Sam (eng-sre): I see repeated segfaults from model-runner on gpu-node-12/13. dmesg shows kernel OOM killer activity shortly before segfaults. Sample tail:```
[ 3191.412345] Out of memory: Kill process 32456 (model-runner) score 820 or sacrifice child
[ 3191.413201] model-runner invoked oom-killer: gfp_mask=0x2080d0
[ 3191.414001] model-runner[32456]: segfault at 7f8d3a0 rw?  rip 00007f8d3c9a1b2 ...
```
Also seeing repeated NVML errors: `GPU 0: out of memory` and `cuCtxSynchronize` failures in the logs. No new deploys in last 12h per deploy bot.

Jit (runtime): Which model and config? Any sudden burst in batch sizing?

Sam (eng-sre): Model: redwood/gptx-8b-ft (quantized int8). Typical batch size 8, but traffic spike pushed ~20 concurrent requests on that node. Memory usage peaked ~96% on GPU.

Maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Reroute traffic off us-west-2 to other regions where capacity is healthy. 2) Fail traffic to smaller fallback variant (gptx-4b-quant) for affected routes. 3) Evict and restart affected pods. 4) Collect cores/coredumps and kernel logs.

Maya (oncall): Running reroute:```sh
# switch route for hosted-api/model/generate to fallback cluster
rbctl route update --service hosted-api --model redwood/gptx-8b-ft --fallback redwood/gptx-4b-quant --region us-west-2
```

ops-bot: command executed: rbctl route update ... -> success.

Sam (eng-sre): Evicting pods now:```sh
kubectl --context usw2 -n inference delete pod model-runner-78f4 --grace-period=10 --force
```
Will rotate the entire node pool if we see repeated OOM after restart.

Jit (runtime): Add a quick runtime fallback to CPU kernels to avoid GPU transient OOM while we stabilize: set env FALLBACK_KERNELS=1 in the deployment and scale down GPU concurrency. Command:```sh
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-runner FALLBACK_KERNELS=1
kubectl -n inference patch hpa model-runner --type merge -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":10}}'
```
Note: CPU fallback increases latency but reduces 5xx.

Emma (support): Status for customers? Which tenants hit errors? We need to craft comms if SLOs impacted.

Maya (oncall): Initial customer impact: 3 active customers reported errors (IDs: cust-8921, cust-4412, cust-2008). Error spikes started ~11:03 UTC. We're rerouting and applying fallback; estimating degraded availability for ~20 minutes.

Sam (eng-sre): Collecting core dumps and enabling ulimit:```sh
# on node
ssh gpu-node-12 'sudo sysctl -w kernel.core_pattern=/var/crash/core.%e.%p'; sudo systemctl stop apport || true
# enable large corefiles
ssh gpu-node-12 'echo "* soft core unlimited" >> /etc/security/limits.conf'
```
I'll rsync cores to /tmp/incident-dumps and post location.

Jit (runtime): Also please capture model runner stack with gdb when process exists:```sh
gdb -batch -ex 'thread apply all bt full' -ex 'quit' /usr/bin/model-runner core.32456 > /tmp/core-32456.bt
```
Share results with me and I'll check kernel-paths and mempinning issues.

Maya (oncall): Update: reroute in effect and fallback model serving accepting traffic. Error rate dropped from 12% -> 2.1% in 7 minutes. Still seeing isolated segfaults on restarted nodes. Patch plan: pin to older CUDA minor version on these nodes and roll forward after test.

Sam (eng-sre): Confirmed dmesg after restart still shows occasional OOM but much less frequent. GPU memory fragmentation appears high; could be driver/CUDA churn. Will coordinate kernel/driver rollback.

Emma (support): Notifying impacted customers with initial blurb: "We're seeing elevated 5xx errors impacting generation in us-west-2, traffic is being routed to fallback model variants while we mitigate. We'll follow up with a timeline and postmortem."

Maya (oncall): Hand-off note: My shift ends in ~2h. Alex is next oncall — @Alex (next-oncall) please take over if anything escalates. Key tasks for next oncall: 1) monitor reroute and confirm stable error rate below 1.5% 2) ensure core uploads complete 3) coordinate driver rollback test in staging before prod roll.

Alex (next-oncall): Acked. I'll be ready to take over. Please leave any pinned logs and the command summary in the incident doc.

ops-bot: status update posted to incident tracker: incident-2026-03-15-1719999999.

Maya (oncall): Quick stats at 11:28 UTC: pre-mitigation 12% 5xx across us-west-2; after reroute + fallback 5xx down to 1.6% in region; customer error reports reduced to one lingering session.

Sam (eng-sre): Follow-ups (post-incident): - reproduce memory fragmentation locally with same model & input distribution - verify CUDA driver revision that introduced fragmentation - add guardrails: lower max-batch-bytes on quantized models, OOM backoff at runtime - add metric: gpu_mem_fragmentation_ratio

Jit (runtime): I'll prepare a hotfix to catch segmentation in the attention kernel and fall back to safer kernel implementation automatically. Will post PR and link.

Maya (oncall): Good work team. Logging this as "mitigated - reroute + fallback" for now. I'll kick off the postmortem and tag relevant owners. If anyone sees a re-escalation, please ping @pagerduty.

Incidents Bot: Incident status changed -> MITIGATED (11:45 UTC). Summary appended to incident tracker.

Maya (oncall): Final note for handoff: core dumps path: s3://incidents/1719999999/cores/, logs: s3://incidents/1719999999/logs/, followups assigned to Sam (eng-sre) and Jit (runtime). Alex take lead on overnight watch.

Alex (next-oncall): Taking handoff. Will monitor through the night.

Maya (oncall): Thanks all, handing over.
